This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.

## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.5`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noVueTemplateKey`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule doesn't have a fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**error**](/reference/diagnostics#error).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`vue`](/linter/domains#vue)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`vue/no-template-key`](https://eslint.vuejs.org/rules/no-template-key)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noVueTemplateKey": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow the `key` attribute on `<template>` elements in Vue.

A `<template>` element groups other elements without adding anything to the page.
Vue uses `key` to tell elements apart when it updates the page, but a `<template>`
isn't an element on the page, so a `key` written on it does nothing.
Put the `key` on the elements inside the `<template>` instead.

A `key` on a `<template>` that also has `v-for` is allowed, because Vue uses that `key`
to keep track of each item in the list.

## Examples

### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <template key="foo"><div /></template>
</template>
```

### Valid

```vue
<template>
  <div key="foo"></div>
  <template v-for="item in list" :key="item.id"><div /></template>
</template>
```
